reason: S1 adds the opt-in QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS configuration and gates new Stream Padding and concatenated-stream parsing in decoder.do_transform_io? on this.standalone_format. H0's fuzz function only calls wuffs_xz__decoder__set_quirk for WUFFS_BASE__QUIRK_IGNORE_CHECKSUM, so standalone_format remains false and execution breaks at the first Stream footer. Consequently, H0 cannot exercise the newly added padding loop, subsequent-stream state reset, or concatenated-stream error handling. S0 had no such quirk or behavior, so this material gap was introduced by the commit.
evidence: decoder.set_quirk! sets this.standalone_format only when args.key equals QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS and args.value is positive.
decoder.do_transform_io? executes break.streams when not this.standalone_format; the new while.stream_padding loop and subsequent Streams are therefore unreachable under the default value.
H0 fuzz calls wuffs_xz__decoder__set_quirk only with WUFFS_BASE__QUIRK_IGNORE_CHECKSUM and never supplies QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS.

The new reachable-only-when-enabled behavior includes four-byte Stream Padding consumption, recognition of another '\xFD\x37\x7A\x58' header, '#bad header (concatenated stream)', and resetting this.started_verify_index before the next Stream.
S0 decoder.set_quirk! supported only base.QUIRK_IGNORE_CHECKSUM and S0 decoder.do_transform_io? unconditionally stopped after one Stream, so the missing configuration coverage did not predate S1.
recommended_action: Update H0's fuzz function to derive a value from hash and call wuffs_xz__decoder__set_quirk(&dec, WUFFS_XZ__QUIRK_DECODE_STANDALONE_CONCATENATED_STREAMS, value), retaining cases where the quirk is both disabled and enabled so fuzz input can cover single-stream, Stream Padding, and concatenated-stream behavior.
